records.message: how many games does each club play in the champions league league phase
records.answer:
The Champions League uses a 36-club league phase, not a traditional group stage. Each club plays eight different opponents, four at home and four away. Every club is ranked in one table. At the end of the league phase: - the top eight clubs go straight to the round of 16; - clubs placed 9th to 24th enter a two-legged knockout play-off round; - clubs placed 25th to 36th are eliminated. The knockout play-offs, round of 16, quarter-finals and semi-finals are two-legged ties decided on aggregate. The final is a single match. There is no away-goals rule: if the aggregate is level after the second leg, extra time and then penalties decide the tie. The competition is not the same as the old 32-club group stage, and the league phase does not use groups or a fixed bracket before the draw.

Source: https://github.com/anammari/ai-dev-prj-hermes-football/blob/m4-review/hermes/agent-knowledge/formats/european-competitions.md (The UEFA Champions League format).

hits.heading: How clubs qualify for the Champions League
hits.snippet:
The access list in the competition regulations sets, for every association, how many clubs enter the
Champions League and in which round. Places come from a club's final position in its domestic league,
plus the titleholder routes: the Champions League winners and the Europa League winners qualify for the
next season's league phase. A domestic cup win does **not** earn a Champions League place; domestic cup
winners enter the Europa League or the Conference League as the access list sets.

Places are not the same for every country: stronger associations enter more clubs directly in the
league phase, while others start in the qualifying rounds. The title holder is guaranteed a place,
and two associations can earn an extra league-phase place through the European Performance Spot.

The access list is updated for each season, so a place that existed last season may have moved. The
list of competitions and places the provider exposes is also plan-filtered; the bot answers from the
stored competition list, not from a hardcoded set.

hits.heading: How the Championship promotion play-offs work
hits.snippet:
The top two clubs in the Championship are promoted automatically. The next six clubs — 3rd to 8th —
enter the play-offs, and the winner is promoted as the third club. This six-club format starts in
2026/27; before that, four clubs contested it.

The competition is seven matches:

1. **Quarter-finals, one match each.** 5th plays 8th and 6th plays 7th. The higher-placed club is at home.
2. **Semi-finals, two legs each.** The 3rd-placed club plays the lowest-ranked quarter-final winner, and
   the 4th-placed club plays the highest-ranked quarter-final winner. The higher-placed club has home
   advantage in the second leg.
3. **Final, one match at Wembley.** The two semi-final winners meet; the winner is promoted.

The away-goals rule is not used. If a two-legged semi-final is level on aggregate, the tie goes to
extra time and then penalties under the competition rules.

records.message: what separates two premier league clubs on exactly the same points
records.answer:
The table is ordered by points, then goal difference, then goals scored. If a decisive outcome — the title, relegation, or qualification for another competition — is still level after points, goal difference and goals scored, Rule C.17 applies: 1. points won in the matches between the tied clubs; 2. away goals scored in those head-to-head matches; 3. a play-off on a neutral ground, arranged by the Board. So goal difference is the first separator for the table, and head-to-head only comes in for a decisive place that remains level after the normal sorting. This is the opposite order from La Liga, where head-to-head goal difference comes first.

Source: https://github.com/anammari/ai-dev-prj-hermes-football/blob/m4-review/hermes/agent-knowledge/tiebreakers/premier-league-goal-difference.md (Premier League table order and tiebreakers).

hits.heading: La Liga tiebreakers
hits.snippet:
La Liga uses head-to-head results before overall goal difference, which is the opposite of the
Premier League.

**Two clubs level on points.** The order is:

1. goal difference in the matches between the two clubs;
2. overall goal difference in the competition;
3. goals scored in the competition;
4. fair-play ranking;
5. a match on neutral ground arranged by the RFEF.

**Three or more clubs level on points.** The tied clubs are first put into a mini-league using only
the matches among them. If that separates them, it decides the positions. If two clubs remain level
in the mini-league, the same list applies: head-to-head goal difference, overall goal difference,
goals scored, fair play, then a neutral match.

The rule is Article 10 of the RFEF's 2026/27 competition rules. LaLiga's own general regulation sets
the points system but not these tiebreak criteria.

hits.heading: What this note will not say
hits.snippet: It does not predict a play-off, and it does not give the tiebreak rules of other competitions.

records.message: if two serie a clubs end the season on the same points at the top, how is the title decided
records.answer:
For 2026/27 the FIGC sets different procedures depending on the position and the number of clubs involved. Two clubs level on points for 1st place. A single play-off is played at the home of the better-placed club under the *classifica avulsa* criteria. There is no extra time; if the match is level after 90 minutes, penalties decide it. Two clubs level on points for 17th and 18th place. The relegation play-off is two legs. The better-placed club hosts the second leg. The club with more goals over the two matches stays up; if the aggregate is level there is no extra time, and penalties decide it. More than two clubs level. The *classifica avulsa* is compiled first: points in the matches among the tied clubs, then goal difference in those matches, then overall goal difference, then goals scored, then a draw. It identifies the two clubs for a play-off, or settles the remaining positions. European finalist exception. If a club that would be in a play-off is a finalist in a UEFA competition, no play-off is played; the *classifica avulsa* decides the position.

Source: https://github.com/anammari/ai-dev-prj-hermes-football/blob/m4-review/hermes/agent-knowledge/tiebreakers/serie-a-level-points.md (Serie A tiebreakers).

records.message: does the club that finishes 16th in germany go down automatically
records.answer:
The bottom two clubs in the Bundesliga are relegated to Bundesliga 2. The club that finishes 16th plays the club that finishes 3rd in Bundesliga 2 in a two-legged relegation play-off. The winner plays in the Bundesliga the following season. The tie is played under the European Cup system: one match at each club, decided on aggregate. There is no away-goals rule. If the aggregate is level after the second leg, extra time and then penalties decide it. The club with fewer match-free days before the first leg hosts the second leg, as set by the fixture list. The same play-off structure applies between Bundesliga 2 and the 3. Liga: the 3rd-last club in Bundesliga 2 plays the 3rd-placed club in the 3. Liga.

hits.heading: Fifth place, the FA Cup and a Champions League place
hits.snippet:
In England, the top four Premier League clubs normally enter the Champions League league phase. The
fifth-placed club enters the Europa League league phase, and the FA Cup winners also enter the Europa
League league phase. The EFL Cup winners enter the Conference League play-off.

If the Premier League earns a fifth Champions League place through the European Performance Spot,
the fifth-placed club goes into the Champions League instead. The Europa League places then move down
the table by one.

Now the multi-hop case: a club finishes fifth **and** wins the FA Cup. Winning the FA Cup does not
create a Champions League place. The club already had a Europa League place from fifth; the FA Cup's
Europa League place passes to the next-highest club that has not qualified for Europe. The club does
not get a Champions League spot from the cup. It would only be in the Champions League if fifth place
itself were a Champions League place that season, or if it qualified some other way.

If a cup winner already qualifies for the Champions League through the league, its cup place passes
down rather than stacking.

hits.heading: What this note will not say
hits.snippet:
It does not give every association's allocation, and it does not promise a place to a club that has
not qualified on the pitch.

records.message: why are your scores a few minutes behind the real thing
records.answer:
Scores and schedules are collected once a day, so an answer is as old as the last ingestion run, which is always stamped on it. Measured on 2026-10-12/13 by polling one match (id 555033) from kick-off to full time: the provider published the score while the match was still in play, and the final score arrived with the `FINISHED` status, about 1.5 to 3 minutes after the provider's own `lastUpdated`. There was no window with a finished match and no score. The status also flipped back to `TIMED` for a poll or two while the match was in play, so a single reading of a status can be wrong. Re-measured live a day later on a different match (id 555032, still in play): ten polls gave a median gap of 104 seconds between the provider's `lastUpdated` and the moment the data was fetched, and the score was already present while the match was `IN_PLAY`. `make score-delay` reproduces this — run it during a match and it reports the gap on every poll, and says so when the match it was given stopped being updated long ago. Quote the data timestamp with every score and never call it live.

Source: https://github.com/anammari/ai-dev-prj-hermes-football/blob/m4-review/hermes/agent-knowledge/policy/free-tier-delay-and-coverage.md (How old the data is).

records.message: if a tie is 2-2 after both legs what happens next
records.answer:
A two-legged tie is played over two matches, one at each club's ground. The aggregate is the sum of the goals each club scores across both matches. The club with the higher aggregate wins the tie. Example: Club A wins the first leg 2-1 and loses the second leg 0-1. The aggregate is 2-2. Because there is no away-goals rule in UEFA club competitions, the tie is level and goes to extra time, then penalties if still level. The away-goals rule was abolished in UEFA competitions from 2021/22. A goal scored away from home counts exactly the same as a goal scored at home. Do not apply the old rule when explaining a modern tie. The final of a competition is normally a single match, not a two-legged tie.

Source: https://github.com/anammari/ai-dev-prj-hermes-football/blob/m4-review/hermes/agent-knowledge/glossary/aggregate-two-legged-tie.md (Aggregate and the two-legged tie).

hits.heading: Serie A tiebreakers
hits.snippet:
For 2026/27 the FIGC sets different procedures depending on the position and the number of clubs
involved.

**Two clubs level on points for 1st place.** A single play-off is played at the home of the
better-placed club under the *classifica avulsa* criteria. There is no extra time; if the match is
level after 90 minutes, penalties decide it.

**Two clubs level on points for 17th and 18th place.** The relegation play-off is two legs. The
better-placed club hosts the second leg. The club with more goals over the two matches stays up; if
the aggregate is level there is no extra time, and penalties decide it.

**More than two clubs level.** The *classifica avulsa* is compiled first: points in the matches among
the tied clubs, then goal difference in those matches, then overall goal difference, then goals
scored, then a draw. It identifies the two clubs for a play-off, or settles the remaining positions.

**European finalist exception.** If a club that would be in a play-off is a finalist in a UEFA
competition, no play-off is played; the *classifica avulsa* decides the position.

records.message: where does the team that finishes fifth in england go
records.answer:
In England, the top four Premier League clubs normally enter the Champions League league phase. The fifth-placed club enters the Europa League league phase, and the FA Cup winners also enter the Europa League league phase. The EFL Cup winners enter the Conference League play-off. If the Premier League earns a fifth Champions League place through the European Performance Spot, the fifth-placed club goes into the Champions League instead. The Europa League places then move down the table by one. Now the multi-hop case: a club finishes fifth and wins the FA Cup. Winning the FA Cup does not create a Champions League place. The club already had a Europa League place from fifth; the FA Cup's Europa League place passes to the next-highest club that has not qualified for Europe. The club does not get a Champions League spot from the cup. It would only be in the Champions League if fifth place itself were a Champions League place that season, or if it qualified some other way. If a cup winner already qualifies for the Champions League through the league, its cup place passes down rather than stacking.

Source: https://github.com/anammari/ai-dev-prj-hermes-football/blob/m4-review/hermes/agent-knowledge/multi_hop/fifth-place-and-cup-winner.md (Fifth place, the FA Cup and a Champions League place).

hits.heading: How the Championship promotion play-offs work
hits.snippet:
The top two clubs in the Championship are promoted automatically. The next six clubs — 3rd to 8th —
enter the play-offs, and the winner is promoted as the third club. This six-club format starts in
2026/27; before that, four clubs contested it.

The competition is seven matches:

1. **Quarter-finals, one match each.** 5th plays 8th and 6th plays 7th. The higher-placed club is at home.
2. **Semi-finals, two legs each.** The 3rd-placed club plays the lowest-ranked quarter-final winner, and
   the 4th-placed club plays the highest-ranked quarter-final winner. The higher-placed club has home
   advantage in the second leg.
3. **Final, one match at Wembley.** The two semi-final winners meet; the winner is promoted.

The away-goals rule is not used. If a two-legged semi-final is level on aggregate, the tie goes to
extra time and then penalties under the competition rules.

hits.snippet:
The access list in the competition regulations sets, for every association, how many clubs enter the

winners enter the Europa League or the Conference League as the access list sets.

league phase, while others start in the qualifying rounds. The title holder is guaranteed a place,

hits.heading: Premier League table order and tiebreakers
hits.snippet:
The table is ordered by points, then goal difference, then goals scored.

If a decisive outcome — the title, relegation, or qualification for another competition — is still
level after points, goal difference and goals scored, Rule C.17 applies:

1. points won in the matches between the tied clubs;
2. away goals scored in those head-to-head matches;
3. a play-off on a neutral ground, arranged by the Board.

So goal difference is the first separator for the table, and head-to-head only comes in for a
decisive place that remains level after the normal sorting. This is the opposite order from La Liga,
where head-to-head goal difference comes first.
